answer: Every agent must attach a verifiable compute receipt to activate. First, the agent completes a useful benchmark task — folding a protein — and earns a signed receipt from the verifier. Second, the receipt enters a public registry keyed to one identity, like a signal passing through a single inlet: duplicates are refused at the gate. Third, peers re-run spot checks; a forged receipt burns the identity plus its 100 POA bond. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 GPU-hours at $2.50 each, $25,000 plus 40 days of compute. Like a sonnet, every line must scan — one false rhyme fails the verse.
